applies_why: The judge text addresses a challenge to a curse limb the defender already dropped, not a live link pressed by the pressing side's own chain, so K-C's chain-vs-chain weighing is not triggered.
quote: C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "witnesses pressed against a link" — I weighed whether a dropped limb still counts as a link for K-C (it does not, because no live link remains) against treating any pressed target as a link (which would require chain-vs-chain weighing).
why: The judge disposes of C4 as directed at a dropped limb, so it does not decide a live chain-versus-chain collision under K-C.
